proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), \(h\), \(k\), and the pilot dimensions.  Condition first on the two pilot releases.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}spline\text{-}population\text{-}algebra}\), their projections lie in the same H\"older balls and ranges as the true nuisances, and, with \(\ell=h/k^{1/d}\), there is \(\vartheta_\tau\) satisfying
\[
 \rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau=\tau_Q(x_0),\qquad
 \lVert R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2
 \le Cb_0,\qquad
 \lVert Q^\circ-Q^0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\ell^{2\alpha},    \tag{12}
\]
where
\[
 b_0=h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha,
 \qquad \lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\lambda_0:=\kappa(1-\kappa),
 \qquad \lVert R^\circ\rVert_2\le C.                          \tag{13}
\]

Put \(x_\eta=\log(8/\eta)\), \(M_h=mh^d\), and
\[
 a_0=\sqrt{\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}\left(1+\frac{k}{M_h}\right)}
 +\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}
 +\frac{\sqrt{k}\,x_\eta^{3/2}}{M_h^{3/2}}
 +\frac{kx_\eta^2}{M_h^2},
\]
\[
 g_0=\frac{\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)x_\eta}}{m\epsilon_n}
       \{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}.                                  \tag{14}
\]
Choose \(C_S\) at least \(\sqrt{C_0}\), where \(C_0\) is from \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}score\text{-}concentration}\).  The assumed inequality \(M_h\ge C_S^2x_\eta\) then permits application of that lemma and gives, conditionally on the pilots, an event \(E_S\) with probability at least \(1-\eta/2\) on which
\[
 \lVert T_*-T_*^\circ\rVert_2\le C a_0.                       \tag{15}
\]

It remains to include the main-block Gaussian release.  Its output dimension \(p_\gamma^2+p_\gamma\) is fixed.  The scalar Gaussian moment-generating identity and a coordinate union bound give
\[
 \Pr\{\lVert Z_*\rVert_2>C\sqrt{x_\eta}\}\le\eta/2.          \tag{16}
\]
Because \(0<\delta_n<1/2\) and \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\),
\[
 c_{\delta_n}\le C\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)},
 \qquad (\epsilon_n^\circ)^{-1}\le2\epsilon_n^{-1}.           \tag{17}
\]
The sensitivity conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), (16), and (17) therefore yield an event \(E_G\), independent of \(E_S\) conditionally on the pilots, such that
\[
 \Pr(E_G\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\ge1-\eta/2,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widetilde T_*-T_*\rVert_2\le Cg_0.                   \tag{18}
\]
On \(E=E_S\cap E_G\), whose conditional probability is at least \(1-\eta\), (15)--(18) imply
\[
 \lVert\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\lVert\widetilde R-R^\circ\rVert_2\le e_0:=C(a_0+g_0).      \tag{19}
\]

We now verify that spectral flooring cannot invalidate the bound.  First suppose
\[
 C\ell^{2\alpha}+e_0\le\lambda_0/2.                            \tag{20}
\]
Equations (12), (19), and the singular-value perturbation inequality give
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(\widetilde Q)\ge\lambda_0/2>lambda_0/4.
\]
Thus the spectral floor is inactive, \(\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}=\widetilde Q\), and \(\lVert\widetilde Q^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_0\).  By (12) and (19),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 &\le \lVert\rho_h(x_0)\rVert_2\lVert\widetilde Q^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert\widetilde R-\widetilde Q\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\\
 &\le C\{b_0+a_0+g_0\}.                                      \tag{21}
 \end{aligned}
\]

If (20) fails, either \(C\ell^{2\alpha}\ge\lambda_0/4\) or \(e_0\ge\lambda_0/4\).  In the first case \(\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\ge c>0\), where \(c\) depends only on the displayed class constants; in the second case \(a_0+g_0\ge c>0\).  Hence in either case
\[
 b_0+a_0+g_0\ge c_*>0.                                       \tag{22}
\]
The singular-value floor always ensures
\[
 \lVert\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le4/\lambda_0.
\]
Together with (13) and (19), this gives on \(E\)
\[
 \left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 \le C\{1+a_0+g_0\}
 \le C'\{b_0+a_0+g_0\},                                      \tag{23}
\]
where the last inequality uses (22) and \(|\tau_Q(x_0)|\le1\).  Choose \(C_B,C_S,C_G\) larger than the constants in both (21) and (23), while retaining \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\).  By the corrected definitions,
\[
 B(h,k)=C_Bb_0,\qquad S(h,k,\eta)=C_Sa_0,\qquad
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)=C_Gg_0.
\]
Thus the asserted error inequality holds on \(E\).  Its conditional failure probability is at most \(\eta\), uniformly in the pilot realization.  Integrating over both pilot blocks proves the unconditional probability bound, including all pilot and main-block Gaussian randomness.

Fix admissible \(h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), the learner and the interval obtained from it by post-processing are replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  For \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), define
\[
 E_Q=\left\{
 \left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 \le B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \right\}.
\]
The proved \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder}\) gives \(\Pr_Q(E_Q)\ge1-\eta\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}pointwise\text{-}identification}\) give
\[
 \tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0).
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) gives \(-1\le\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\le1\).  Hence, on \(E_Q\), the common value belongs both to the untruncated radius interval and to \([-1,1]\), and therefore
\[
 E_Q\subseteq\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}.
\]
Taking probabilities and then the infimum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) yields
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
All probabilities above integrate the three sample blocks and all three independent Gaussian releases, because the conditional pilot argument in \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder}\) was integrated before it was invoked here.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), and condition on any projected pilot pair \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\) produced by \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\).  Let \(\Pi_{h,k}\) denote componentwise Lebesgue \(L^2(C_h)\)-projection onto the span of \(b_{h,k}\).  There is a coefficient vector \(\vartheta_\tau\in\mathbb R^{p_\gamma}\) such that, with
\[
 g=\pi_Q-\bar\pi,\qquad r=\mu_{0,Q}-\bar\mu,
 \qquad t=\tau_Q-\rho_h^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau,
\]
one has \(\rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau=\tau_Q(x_0)\), \(\lVert\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\le C\), and \(\lVert t\rVert_{L^\infty(C_h)}\le Ch^\gamma\).  If \((Q^\circ,R^\circ)=\mathbb E_Q[(T_{*,Q},T_{*,R})\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu]\) and
\[
 Q^0=\int_{C_h}K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\rho_h(x)^{\mathsf T}
       \pi_Q(x)\{1-\pi_Q(x)\}\,dx,
\]
then
\[
 R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau
 =\int_{C_h}K_h\rho_h\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)t\,dx
 +\int_{C_h}(I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_h g)
                 (I-\Pi_{h,k})(r+\pi_Qt)\,dx,
\]
and
\[
 Q^\circ-Q^0
 =\int_{C_h}(I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_h g)
                 (I-\Pi_{h,k})(\pi_Q\rho_h^{\mathsf T})\,dx.
\]
Consequently, with \(\ell_{h,k}=h/k^{1/d}\),
\[
 \lVert R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2
 \le C\{h^\gamma+\ell_{h,k}^{\alpha+\beta}
                  +h^\gamma\ell_{h,k}^\alpha\},
 \qquad
 \lVert Q^\circ-Q^0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{2\alpha}.
\]
Moreover, \(\lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\kappa(1-\kappa)\) and \(\lVert R^\circ\rVert_2\le C\).  Every constant in this lemma depends only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, not on the pilot dimensions or their realized Gaussian noises.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}propensity\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}holder}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}cate\text{-}holder}\) hold.  The metric projections in \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) therefore give
\[
 \bar\pi\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L_\pi;\mathcal X),\quad
 \kappa\le\bar\pi\le1-\kappa,
 \qquad
 \bar\mu\in\mathcal H^\beta(L_\mu;\mathcal X),\quad
 0\le\bar\mu\le1.
\]
In particular, \(g\in\mathcal H^\alpha(2L_\pi;\mathcal X)\) and \(r\in\mathcal H^\beta(2L_\mu;\mathcal X)\).  These conclusions are deterministic after conditioning on the pilots.

Let \(P_\tau\) be the Taylor polynomial of order \(\lfloor\gamma\rfloor\) of the H\"older version of \(\tau_Q\) at \(x_0\), expressed in the tensor Legendre coordinates \(\rho_h\); its coordinate vector is \(\vartheta_\tau\).  Taylor's formula with H\"older remainder gives
\[
 P_\tau(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0),\qquad
 \sup_{x\in C_h}|\tau_Q(x)-P_\tau(x)|\le C L_\tau h^\gamma,
 \qquad \lVert\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\le C.
\]
The last bound uses bounded outcomes, which imply \(|\tau_Q|\le1\), and equivalence of norms in the fixed-dimensional polynomial space.

We next compute the population score.  Conditional on \(X=x\), consistency and the definitions of \(\mu_{0,Q}\) and \(\tau_Q\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_Q(Y\mid A,X=x)=\mu_{0,Q}(x)+A\tau_Q(x).
\]
Using \(A^2=A\), one obtains, pointwise in \(x\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Q\!\left[(A-\bar\pi)
       \{Y-\bar\mu-A\rho_h^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau\}\mid X=x\right]
 =\pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)t+gr.
\]
Since \(\pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)=\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)+\pi_Qg\), this is
\[
 \pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)t+g(r+\pi_Qt).                                      \tag{1}
\]
The clipping maps in the definition of \(T_*\) are identities on the realized kernels, because their radii are the suprema over the ranges containing \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\).  Independence of the two records in the order-two kernel and the orthonormality of \(b_{h,k}\) show that its population contribution to the last product in (1) is
\[
 \int_{C_h}\Pi_{h,k}(K_h\rho_hg)\,
                  \Pi_{h,k}(r+\pi_Qt)\,dx.
\]
Self-adjointness and idempotence of \(\Pi_{h,k}\) give the Pythagorean identity
\[
 \int uv-\int(\Pi_{h,k}u)(\Pi_{h,k}v)
 =\int\{(I-\Pi_{h,k})u\}\{(I-\Pi_{h,k})v\}.              \tag{2}
\]
Substituting \(u=K_h\rho_hg\) and \(v=r+\pi_Qt\) into (2) proves the first displayed identity.  Applying the same calculation to the matrix score, and using
\[
 \pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)=\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)+\pi_Qg,
\]
proves the identity for \(Q^\circ-Q^0\).

It remains to bound the two remainders.  The resolution-ordered boundary-corrected tensor spline system in the corrected declaration of \(b_{h,k}\) has mesh width comparable to \(\ell_{h,k}=h/k^{1/d}\).  To verify the needed approximation rather than assume it, partition the rescaled unit cube at the last complete resolution preceding the \(k\)-th basis function.  On each tensor cell subtract the Taylor polynomial of order \(\lfloor u\rfloor\) of a function \(v\in\mathcal H^u(L;C_h)\).  The H\"older remainder is at most \(CL\ell_{h,k}^u\); the polynomial lies in the spline space because its coordinatewise order is below the declared spline order.  Squaring and integrating over the \(h^d\)-volume cube, and then using the best-approximation property of orthogonal projection, gives
\[
 \lVert(I-\Pi_{h,k})v\rVert_2
 \le CLh^{d/2}\ell_{h,k}^u.                                  \tag{3}
\]
For \(K_h\rho_hv\), perform the same cellwise subtraction after multiplying the Taylor polynomial by \(\rho_h\).  The product remains in the declared spline space, and \(K_h=h^{-d}\) on \(C_h\), whence
\[
 \lVert(I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hv)\rVert_2
 \le CLh^{-d/2}\ell_{h,k}^u.                                 \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4), Cauchy--Schwarz, and contraction of an orthogonal projection yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left\lVert\int (I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hg)
                  (I-\Pi_{h,k})r\,dx\right\rVert_2
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{\alpha+\beta},\\
 &\left\lVert\int (I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hg)
                  (I-\Pi_{h,k})(\pi_Qt)\,dx\right\rVert_2
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{\alpha}\lVert\pi_Qt\rVert_2h^{-d/2}
 \le Ch^\gamma\ell_{h,k}^\alpha,\\
 &\left\lVert\int (I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hg)
                  (I-\Pi_{h,k})(\pi_Q\rho_h^{\mathsf T})\,dx
   \right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{2\alpha}.
 \end{aligned}                                                \tag{5}
\]
The first integral in the score identity is bounded by \(Ch^\gamma\), since \(\int K_h=1\), \(\rho_h\) is uniformly bounded, and \(0\le\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)\le1/4\).  This proves the two asserted remainder bounds.

Finally, the canonical tensor Legendre normalization gives
\[
 \int_{C_h}K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\rho_h(x)^{\mathsf T}\,dx=I_{p_\gamma}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\) therefore implies
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}Q^0v
 \ge\kappa(1-\kappa)\int K_h(v^{\mathsf T}\rho_h)^2
 =\kappa(1-\kappa)\lVert v\rVert_2^2.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\kappa(1-\kappa)\).  The bound on \(R^\circ\) follows either directly from the range restrictions, (2), and projection contraction, or from \(R^\circ=Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau+(R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau)\), the already proved bounds, and \(0<\ell_{h,k}\le h\le r_0\le1/4\).

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The order-two projection statistic has conditional-square and sup-norm moment diagrams of orders \(\sqrt{k}\,x_\eta^{3/2}/(mh^d)^{3/2}\) and \(k x_\eta^2/(mh^d)^2\).  They are not uniformly absorbed by the frozen sub-Gaussian term under only \(mh^d\ge C_S^2x_\eta\).  Adding them gives the finite-sample envelope actually proved; for fixed noncoverage they are lower order under \(k\le mh^d\), so the polynomial rate is unchanged.

proposed_core_edits.name: b

proposed.name: b
proposed.type: \(b_{h,k}\) is the vector of the first \(k\) functions, in resolution order, of a boundary-corrected orthonormal tensor-product spline-wavelet basis on the cube centered at \(x_0\) with side length \(h\); its regularity and vanishing moments exceed \(\lfloor\gamma\rfloor+\lceil\max\{\alpha,\beta\}\rceil\), and it is zero off that cube

proposed_core_edits.reason: The rate \((h/k^{1/d})^u\) for \(u\in\{\alpha,\beta\}\) is not implied by an order-unspecified spline label when \(u>1\).  The replacement fixes the estimator's deterministic basis design at sufficient order; the population lemma derives the Jackson bounds from this construction rather than assuming them as law conditions.

proposed.statement:
There are constants \(C_B,C_S,C_G\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, such that for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), every \(0<h\le r_0\), and every \(1\le k\le m h^d\) with \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), the projected private pilots satisfy the same H\"older-radius and range restrictions as the primitive nuisances and
\[
 \Pr_Q\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|>
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\right\}\le\eta.
\]
The three displayed summands respectively bound localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation of the linear and degenerate terms, and all propagated Gaussian release noise.
proposed.justification: A uniform error envelope prevents coverage from being inferred by simply adding a Gaussian variance to a biased nonregular estimator.
proposed.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 gives an expected-error decomposition without privacy or coverage; ArmstrongKolesar2020 treats worst-case smoothing bias without causal higher-order nuisance bias.
proposed.consumer: The bound gives investigators a finite-sample radius that remains valid when low nuisance smoothness makes first-order CATE intervals undercover.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof spine now exposes the exact projected-score cancellation and the finite-sample order-two concentration calculation as load-bearing lemmas.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 \ell=hk^{-1/d},\quad
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},\quad
 r_2=n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q)\}},
\]
and let
\[
 t=r_{\mathrm{up}}
   =r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}.
\]
We first reduce the three envelopes to a form convenient for tuning.  The constraints
\(1\le k\le mh^d\) imply
\[
 m^{-1/d}\le \ell\le h\le r_0\le 1/4.
\]
Since \(n\ge12\) and \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\),
\[
 n/4\le m\le n/3.
\]
Consequently, Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\),
\(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and
\(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\), together with
\(\sqrt{a+b}\le\sqrt a+\sqrt b\) for \(a,b\ge0\), give a constant
\(C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\), such that
\[
 B(h,k)
 =C_B\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}
 \le C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q\},                                      \tag{1}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(\ell\le1\) and \(\alpha>0\),
\[
\begin{split}
 S(h,k,\eta)
 &\le C\left\{n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
       +n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}\right\},                       \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]
where \(k^{1/2}=h^{d/2}\ell^{-d/2}\), and
\[
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}
       \{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\}.                               \tag{3}
\]
For (3), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) gives
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}
 ={\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)\log(1/\eta)}\over n\epsilon_n},
\]
while the ratio between the logarithmic factor in the privacy envelope and the
one in this display is
\(\sqrt{\log(8/\eta)/\log(1/\eta)}\); also \(n/m\le4\).
Thus the constant in (3) is uniform in \(n,\epsilon_n,\delta_n\).

We next rewrite the privacy-free rate.  Since \(s=q/2\), the first branch in
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) is \(r_2\), and its branch
condition is
\[
 q<{d\over2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.                                   \tag{4}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 1+{d\over2\gamma}+{d\over2q}>2+{d\over\gamma}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q<{d\over2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
\]
Because \(n>1\), this comparison of denominators proves, including equality at
the boundary in (4), that
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2.                                    \tag{5}
\]

We construct a feasible comparison pair \((h,k)\).  All constants used in this
construction are fixed independently of \(n,\epsilon_n,\delta_n\).  First
suppose \(q<\gamma\).  With
\[
 a_q={1\over1+d/\gamma+d/q},
\]
the corrected definition has \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-a_q}\).
The restrictions \(\epsilon_n\le1\) and \(\delta_n<1/2\) imply
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}
 \le {n\over\sqrt{\log 2\,\log(1/\eta)}}=:C_\eta n.              \tag{6}
\]
As \(a_q\le q/d\), equations (6) and \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) imply
\[
 t^{1/q}\ge C_1 n^{-1/d}\ge C_2m^{-1/d}                         \tag{7}
\]
for positive constants \(C_1,C_2\).  Choose a fixed \(A\ge C_2^{-1}\), and set
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\quad \ell_0=A t^{1/q},\quad
 k=\left\lfloor (h/\ell_0)^d\right\rfloor.                       \tag{8}
\]
There is a fixed \(t_0\in(0,1)\) such that, whenever \(t<t_0\),
the inequality \(q<\gamma\) makes \(\ell_0\le h\), so \(k\ge1\).
Equation (7) and the choice of \(A\) give
\[
 k\le(h/\ell_0)^d\le mh^d.                                      \tag{9}
\]
If \(K=(h/\ell_0)^d\ge1\), then
\(\lfloor K\rfloor\ge K/2\).  Hence the actual value
\(\ell=hk^{-1/d}\) satisfies
\[
 \ell_0\le\ell\le2^{1/d}\ell_0.                                \tag{10}
\]
Integer rounding therefore changes every ensuing bound by only a fixed factor.

The four fluctuation inequalities required in (2)--(3) follow directly from
the four components of \(t\).  Indeed, by (5),
\[
\begin{split}
 t\ge r_o
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 n^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le t,\\
 t\ge r_2
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}\le t.                              \tag{11}
\end{split}
\]
Also, because
\(r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)}\) and
\(r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}\),
\[
\begin{split}
 t\ge r_{\mathrm{reg}}
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,\\
 t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.                  \tag{12}
\end{split}
\]
Substitution of (8)--(12) into (1)--(3) yields
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le C t.      \tag{13}
\]
The remaining feasibility requirements also hold uniformly for all sufficiently
large \(n\).  In fact, \(t\ge r_o\) gives
\[
 mh^d=mt^{d/\gamma}
 \ge {1\over4}n^{\,2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\longrightarrow\infty,    \tag{14}
\]
so (14) eventually implies
\(mh^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\).  By decreasing \(t_0\), if necessary,
we also have \(h\le r_0\).  Equations (9) and (14) now verify every stated
constraint.

Suppose instead that \(q\ge\gamma\).  For \(t<t_0\), take
\[
 k=1,\quad h=t^{1/\gamma},\quad \ell=h.                            \tag{15}
\]
Then \(h^q\le h^\gamma=t\).  The first term in (2) is at most \(Ct\)
by \(t\ge r_o\).  The second term in (2) is
\[
 n^{-1}h^{-d}
 =\{n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}\}^2\le t^2\le t.                            \tag{16}
\]
Here \(\bar q=\gamma\), so the corrected definition gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}
 =N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-2d}\le t,                             \tag{17}
\]
and, since \(h\le1\), (17) also bounds
\(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-d}\).  Equations (1)--(3) and
(15)--(17) again prove (13).  Feasibility follows from (14), now with \(k=1\),
and from \(h\le r_0\).  This calculation also identifies the two advertised
privacy regimes: (12) is the \(q\)-branch when \(q<\gamma\), whereas (17) is
the private-Gram rate \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\)
when \(q\ge\gamma\).

It remains to justify minimization and the case in which the rate is not small.
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \((h,k)=(r_0,1)\) is feasible, so the feasible
set is nonempty.  For each feasible integer \(k\), its admissible bandwidths
form a closed subinterval of \((0,r_0]\), bounded away from zero by
\[
 h\ge\max\left\{(k/m)^{1/d},
 \{C_S^2\log(8/\eta)/m\}^{1/d}\right\}.
\]
There are only finitely many possible integers \(k\le mr_0^d\), and the objective
is continuous in \(h\) on each such interval.  Hence a deterministic minimizer
exists.  When \(t<t_0\), its objective is no larger than (13).  When
\(t\ge t_0\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\)
gives \(C_n(h,k)\subseteq[-1,1]\), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}\le2\le (2/t_0)t.              \tag{18}
\]
When \(t<t_0\), the same definition and nonnegativity of the three envelopes give
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}
 \le2R_n(h,k)
 =2\{B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\}
 \le2Ct.                                                          \tag{19}
\]
The bounds (18)--(19) are pointwise in the realized sample and do not involve
the pilot dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\).  Taking expectation under each
\(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) and then the supremum over that class proves
the asserted inequality with \(C_L=\max\{2C,2/t_0\}\).  All lower bounds on
\(n\) used in feasibility depend only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\),
which yields the stated \(n_0\).
